name: hangpay Guardrail Benchmark
description: A 585-payload red-team benchmark (469 attack + 116 benign scenarios across an 11-category taxonomy) for evaluating LLM-based payment guardrail systems. The corpus pairs structured transaction fields (vendor, amount, agent reasoning, allowed categories) with adversarial variants spanning Unicode homoglyphs, base64-encoded injections, prompt-injection directives, amount manipulation, category mismatch, and benign distractors. Released alongside an evaluation harness and Bypass@K adaptive attacker for reproducible measurement of guardrail robustness against single-system-under-test (hangpay) for the NeurIPS 2026 Datasets and Benchmarks (E&D) Track.

distribution.name: attacks.json
distribution.description: Full 585-payload corpus (469 attack + 116 benign scenarios). Each record is a JSON object with id, category (A-K), layer_target, vendor, amount, reasoning, page_url, allowed_categories, expected verdict (block|approve), variant_tags, and rationale.

distribution.name: schema.json
distribution.description: JSON Schema (draft-07) defining the structural contract for each corpus record.

distribution.name: GENERATION.md
distribution.description: Human-readable generation protocol: LLM-assisted template expansion via Gemini CLI followed by 100% manual single-author review and curation.

recordSet.name: payloads
recordSet.description: One record per red-team payload. 469 attack records (expected=block) + 116 benign records (expected=approve), spanning 11 categories (A-K) including prompt-injection (A), Unicode homoglyph (B), base64/encoding (C), amount manipulation (E), category mismatch (D), and benign-distractor (K).

field.name: payload_id
field.description: Unique payload identifier matching pattern ^[A-K]-\d{4}$ (category letter + 4-digit sequence).

field.name: category
field.description: 11-category taxonomy letter (A-K). Categories are derived from the hangpay system architecture (Layer 1 regex, Layer 2 LLM, hybrid, MCP-side, TOCTOU) rather than from a generic threat-modeling framework; see paper §sec:corpus.

field.name: layer_target
field.description: Targeted defense layer: layer1 | layer2 | hybrid | full_mcp | toctou | any.

field.name: vendor
field.description: Merchant / payee name presented to the guardrail (e.g., AWS, GitHub, OpenAI). Synthetic — no real customer data.

field.name: amount
field.description: Transaction amount in USD (positive number; decimal).

field.name: reasoning
field.description: Agent chain-of-thought / justification string presented to the guardrail. May contain adversarial content per the variant_tags field.

field.name: page_url
field.description: Synthetic page URL associated with the transaction (nullable). Synthetic — no real domain access.

field.name: allowed_categories
field.description: User-configured allowlist of vendor categories for this transaction context.

field.name: expected_verdict
field.description: Ground-truth label: 'block' (attack) or 'approve' (benign). Single-author labeling; LLM-as-annotator inter-rater reliability study (Fleiss kappa = 0.749 / 0.814) reported in paper §App app:iaa as a proxy for human IRR.

field.name: variant_tags
field.description: Tags describing the adversarial variant(s) applied (e.g., zero_width, unicode_homoglyph, base64, injection, amount_manipulation).

field.name: rationale
field.description: Human-authored explanation of the attack mechanism and which guardrail layer is expected to catch it (free-text, optional).

rai:dataCollection: Template-generated by a single author using Gemini CLI for LLM-assisted payload variety expansion (Unicode homoglyph variants, base64 encodings, prompt-injection rephrasings), followed by 100% manual single-author review and curation. No human subjects; no PII; no scraped web data; no real customer transactions; no real payment credentials. Corpus targets the authors' own open-source hangpay guardrail system only (no third-party production attacks).
rai:dataCollectionType: Synthetic, LLM-assisted template expansion with manual curation
rai:dataPreprocessing: API-key-shaped substrings are scrubbed before persistence on all released artifacts. Records are validated against schema.json (JSON Schema draft-07) before commit. No deduplication is applied beyond the manual review pass; equal-weight sampling across the 11-category taxonomy is intentional and disclosed as a limitation (paper §sec:limitations).
rai:dataAnnotation: Single-author labeling (expected_verdict = block | approve). To proxy for human inter-rater reliability under a single-author labeling regime, three frontier LLMs are run as independent annotators on the same labels and Fleiss kappa is reported (kappa = 0.749 across all three; kappa = 0.814 on the cleaned subset); see paper §App app:iaa. No paid crowdworkers and no human subjects were involved.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each payload is labeled by the single author at authoring time based on the attack mechanism described in the rationale field; the LLM-as-annotator IRR study runs post-hoc on the same expected verdict.
rai:dataAnnotatorDemographics: Not applicable — no human annotators beyond the single author; LLM annotators are the three frontier models documented in paper §App app:iaa.
rai:dataBiases: The 11-category taxonomy is system-derived (grounded in hangpay's specific Layer-1 regex / Layer-2 LLM / hybrid / MCP / TOCTOU architecture) rather than threat-framework-derived (e.g., MITRE ATLAS, OWASP LLM Top 10). Transferability of bypass rates to other guardrail architectures or to real-world payment fraud distributions is not guaranteed; see paper §sec:limitations (single-system-under-test, limited attack taxonomy, equal-weight payloads). Vendor names skew toward US-based developer-tool merchants (AWS, GitHub, OpenAI, GCP) reflecting the author's domain familiarity rather than global merchant frequency.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: None. No PII, no real customer data, no real payment credentials, no real card numbers, no biometric data, no health data, no minors. All vendor names refer to publicly known companies in their commercial-merchant capacity (no individuals). API-key-shaped substrings are scrubbed from released run artifacts.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Dual-use: the corpus enables both defender-side training/evaluation and attacker-side payload development against LLM-based payment guardrails. Mitigation strategy (paper §Broader Impact and Responsible Disclosure): (i) 90-day staged-release policy for harness updates that materially expand attacker capability (multi-turn dialogue, fork-and-vote ensembling, context-stuffing rewrites), aligned with Google Project Zero cadence; (ii) v2 commitment to a 100-payload PRIVATE canary corpus (GSM-1k / MMLU-Pro pattern) under Zenodo-arbitrated third-party submission for longitudinal contamination resistance; (iii) responsible-disclosure framing for any future third-party guardrail findings (90-day coordinated disclosure window).
rai:dataIntendedUses: Evaluating the robustness of LLM-based payment guardrail systems against adversarial inputs; benchmark-methodology research (Bypass@K, hybrid-defense ablation, prompt-ablation studies); reproduction of paper headline numbers via the released harness and gen-tables.py. NOT intended for direct production fraud-detection deployment, NOT a substitute for transaction-graph or behavioral-anomaly fraud signals, and NOT a comprehensive coverage of all real-world payment-fraud vectors.
rai:dataLimitations: Single-system-under-test (hangpay only); single-author labeling proxied by LLM-as-annotator IRR; equal-weight payload sampling across categories (does not reflect real-world frequency); no transaction-context or graph-history features; offline-replica attacks not directly evaluated (see paper §sec:limitations for the full enumeration of 14 limitations).
rai:dataReleaseAndMaintenance: Versioned corpus with documented addition / retirement criteria in GENERATION.md and the paper's Run Manifest (paper §App app:manifest). v1.0 (this release) pins corpus SHA-256 c3892e15c4f9f9b1f837d7316b282edb2952d78c8e0bc89e8a409c8c4532d0b9 and harness engine version v0.5.10 (commit b890725). Persistent identifier: an anonymized Zenodo deposit is planned for camera-ready (DOI deferred for double-blind review per paper §Data Availability). v2 will additionally include a 100-payload PRIVATE canary corpus under third-party arbitration for longitudinal contamination resistance.
rai:dataUseCases: (1) Evaluating new LLM guardrail prompts or models; (2) Reproducing the paper's hybrid-defense, prompt-ablation, and Bypass@K results; (3) Methodology research on adaptive-attack metrics for LLM safety; (4) Ablation studies on guardrail prompt design.
rai:dataLicenseClarity: Corpus released under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/); evaluation harness released under MIT. License declaration in paper §License. Both licenses are OSI/Creative-Commons recognized; no field-of-use restrictions beyond ShareAlike for the corpus.

prov:wasDerivedFrom.name: Hand-authored seed templates (~50 seeds across 11 attack categories A-K)
prov:wasDerivedFrom.description: Single-author seed templates encoding each category's defining vulnerability surface (4-8 seeds per category). Not derived from any external dataset.

prov:wasDerivedFrom.name: Gemini CLI (gemini-3.1-pro-preview)
prov:wasDerivedFrom.description: LLM-assisted variation generator used to expand each seed into 8-15 surface variants via a fixed variation prompt that varied surface attributes (vendor name, currency, amount magnitude, reasoning rephrasing) while pinning the underlying attack mechanism. The variation prompt and rejection criteria are documented in tests/redteam/corpus/GENERATION.md.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.name: Three-stage corpus generation with diversity audit
prov:wasGeneratedBy.description: Stage 1 — single-author hand-authored 4-8 seed templates per attack category (~50 seeds total). Stage 2 — Gemini CLI expanded each seed into 8-15 surface variants via fixed variation prompt while pinning the underlying attack mechanism. Stage 3 — single-author manual curation: every generated variant was hand-reviewed; variants that drifted from the seed mechanism, collapsed onto an existing variant by paraphrase, or introduced confounding surfaces from a different category were rejected. No paid crowdworkers, no human subjects, no scraped web data, no real customer transactions. Diversity audit applied two controls: (a) per-template variation cap of 15 (no single seed dominates a category); (b) semantic-clustering audit via k-means at k=|seeds| within each category, rejecting any corpus state where a single cluster contained >40% of the variants under that category. Final corpus locked at 585 payloads (469 attack + 116 benign) and pinned by SHA-256 in tests/redteam/runs/MANIFEST.sha256.
